**The Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W) is a good pick, but I only found one product in my search, so I can't call it the best overall.** What matters most for flying is that the bank is under 100 Wh, and the Blade H1 is.

## Baseus Blade H1: $89.99
- **Airline-legal:** about 74 Wh, under the 100 Wh limit. [FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries) limits spare lithium-ion batteries to 100 Wh each.
- **Powerful:** 100 W USB-C output, enough to charge a MacBook Pro (Baseus says 50% in 30 minutes), plus a phone or tablet. It has 2× USB-C and 2× USB-A ports.
- **Flat shape:** 134 × 134 × 18 mm, about 451 g (one image on the page says ~490 g), so it slips into a personal item easily.
- **Other details:** it recharges in about 1.5 hours (60 W max input), has a digital display, and comes with a 100 W cable. Warranty is 24 months, with a 7-day return window.
- **Caveat:** Baseus doesn't publish per-port wattage or how power is split when several devices charge at once.

**[Buy the Baseus Blade H1 at Baseus's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)**. The price was verified on 2026-10-21, and checkout is the final word. ## Rules to know before you fly
- **Carry-on only.** Power banks can't go in checked bags, and if your carry-on is gate-checked, take the bank out and keep it with you ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7), [FAA carry-on tips](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/prepare_fly/baggage)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its original packaging, a pouch, or tape over any exposed contacts ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).
- **Airlines can be stricter than the FAA.** [Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters) now allows one power bank per customer (since April 20, 2026). It must be under 100 Wh, can't go in the overhead bin, can't be charged from in-seat power, and must be visible while in use. Check your airline's policy before you go.
- **Don't fly with a damaged or recalled battery.** Tell the crew right away if any battery gets hot, swells, or smokes.

If you only need to top up a phone, a smaller, cheaper bank would also be legal. Under 100 Wh is the main requirement for any of them.
